Build a document network

Source: R/document-network.R
document_network.Rd

document_network() builds a network between documents (papers) in the dataset. By default two documents are linked by bibliographic coupling, when they share cited references (Kessler, 1963); the other types are direct citation, co-citation of the cited items (Small, 1973) and the cosine similarity of the documents' reference vectors.

Usage

document_network(
  data,
  type = "coupling",
  counting = "full",
  similarity = "none",
  threshold = 0,
  min_occur = 1L,
  top_n = NULL,
  self_loops = FALSE,
  deduplicate = TRUE,
  format = "edgelist",
  references = "references",
  sep = ";",
  strip_quotes = TRUE,
  id = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per work and a references column (list-column or delimited string). An id column is optional (see id); direct citation needs the references to use the same identifiers.

type

Character. Relationship type:

"coupling"

Bibliographic coupling: documents linked when they share cited references.

"citation"

Direct citation: directed edges from citing to cited documents (internal citations only). counting, similarity, threshold and min_occur are not applied; top_n keeps the documents with the most citation edges.

"co_citation"

Co-citation of the cited items: the nodes are the values of the references column (as in reference_network()), linked when the same document cites both. They are documents of the dataset only when the references are document identifiers.

"equivalence"

Cosine similarity of the documents' reference vectors; counting and similarity are ignored.

counting

Character. Counting method: "full" (default), "fractional", "paper" or "strength". Position-dependent methods are not applicable to document networks.

similarity

Character. Similarity measure. Default "none".

threshold

Numeric. Minimum edge weight; edges with weight < threshold are dropped. Default 0 (keep all).

min_occur

Integer. Minimum reference frequency. Default 1.

top_n

Integer or NULL. Keep only the top_n most frequent nodes and return the edges among them. Default NULL (all nodes).

self_loops

Logical. If TRUE, include self-loops (an entity linked to itself). Default FALSE. Only takes effect with similarity = "none"; every similarity measure zeroes the diagonal.

deduplicate

Logical. If TRUE (default), each (paper, entity) pair is counted at most once – duplicate entries in the source data (e.g., the same author listed twice on a paper) are treated as one occurrence. Set to FALSE to count every raw occurrence.

format

Character. Output format:

"edgelist"

Default. A bibnets_network data frame with columns from, to, weight, count.

"gephi"

Gephi-ready data frame: Source, Target, Weight, Count, Type.

"igraph"

An igraph graph object (requires igraph).

"cograph"

A cograph_network object (requires cograph).

"matrix"

A sparse adjacency matrix.

references

Character. Name of the column containing cited references. Default "references".

sep

Character. Separator used to split the references column when it is a plain character column. Default ";". Ignored for list-columns.

strip_quotes

Logical. If TRUE (default), surrounding quote characters are removed from each reference.

id

Optional. Name of the column to use as the work identifier (the matrix-row dimension). If NULL (default), an existing id column is used when present, otherwise row numbers are used.

Value

Depends on format. The default "edgelist" returns a bibnets_network data frame with one row per edge, columns from, to, weight and count, and attributes network_type, counting and similarity; see author_network() for the other formats. For type = "citation" the edges are directed (from = citing, to = cited) with weight and count both 1, in data order; the other types are undirected and sorted by decreasing weight.

Details

The documents and their references form a two-mode matrix, projected onto the documents for coupling and onto the cited items for co-citation; counting and similarity weight the edges and threshold, min_occur and top_n prune them. It returns a bibnets_network edge list by default, directed for type = "citation". For a co-citation network of the references themselves see reference_network(); for local citation counts and a chronological citation network see local_citations() and historiograph().

References

Kessler, M. M. (1963). Bibliographic coupling between scientific papers. American Documentation, 14(1), 10–25. doi:10.1002/asi.5090140103

Small, H. (1973). Co-citation in the scientific literature: A new measure of the relationship between two documents. Journal of the American Society for Information Science, 24(4), 265–269. doi:10.1002/asi.4630240406

Examples

data(biblio_data)
document_network(biblio_data, "coupling")
#> # bibnets network: document_coupling | 10 nodes · 36 edges | counting: full 
#>     from  to  weight  count
#>  1  W4    W9       4      4
#>  2  W1    W3       3      3
#>  3  W4    W6       3      3
#>  4  W1    W7       3      3
#>  5  W6    W9       3      3
#>  6  W1    W2       2      2
#>  7  W2    W3       2      2
#>  8  W2    W4       2      2
#>  9  W3    W4       2      2
#> 10  W2    W5       2      2
#> # ... 26 more edges
document_network(biblio_data, "coupling", counting = "strength")
#> # bibnets network: document_coupling | 10 nodes · 36 edges | counting: strength 
#>     from  to   weight  count
#>  1  W4    W9   0.1981      4
#>  2  W1    W7   0.1938      3
#>  3  W1    W3   0.1619      3
#>  4  W6    W10  0.1579      2
#>  5  W4    W6   0.1229      3
#>  6  W5    W8   0.1229      2
#>  7  W6    W9   0.1229      3
#>  8  W1    W2   0.1186      2
#>  9  W2    W7   0.1186      2
#> 10  W3    W7   0.1186      2
#> # ... 26 more edges
